transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I just can't seem to keep my work straight lately. I work at a dry cleaner, and it's just... tickets, receipts, customer jobs, little notes... they all just end up in a pile. I look at it and I don't even know where to start anymore. It's just a mess.
Have you struggled with this kind of disorganization and difficulty getting started on tasks since you were a child, or is this a more recent problem for you?

It's... not really new, no. I guess it's been like this for a long time. 

Even back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was bright, but... scattered. I'd lose my school papers a lot. I guess I was always talking out of turn, too... and they always had to remind me to just finish my work. So, yeah. It's been a while.
Do you often feel like you have to be on the go or that you have trouble sitting still for long periods, like during meetings or while watching a movie?

I suppose... yeah. I don't really sit well for that long. 

Like, if I have to go to a church committee meeting, or... those fabric-care trainings for work. I usually end up finding some reason to get up. Just to go get water, or... check on some papers. I just keep getting up, even when everybody else is just sitting there.

When you look back at your struggles, would you say that being unable to pay close attention to details or making careless mistakes is more of a problem for you than the feeling of needing to be constantly on the go?
I'm not really sure which one is worse, honestly. They both just kind of... happen. I don't know that I could pick one over the other.

When you are in those meetings or training sessions, do you often find yourself blurting out answers before the speaker has finished their question, or do you find it hard to wait your turn in conversation?

I guess I do that sometimes. 

If my daughter is talking, or... a customer at the counter, or the trainer at work. I just... jump in. Before they even finish asking. And then, half the time, I realize I didn't even answer what they were actually going to ask. It just... slips out.
Do you find that these difficulties with staying organized and sitting still happen at home just as often as they do at work?
I don't know. I guess so. It's just... kind of everywhere, really.

Looking back over the last six months, would you say that you have frequently struggled with both being disorganized and forgetful, AND being restless and impulsive, or is one of those two categories clearly more dominant for you?
I couldn't really tell you. I haven't... kept track, I guess. It all just kind of blends together.

If you had to look at a checklist of common symptoms, would you say you experience at least six distinct symptoms of inattention—like losing things or being distracted—AND at least six distinct symptoms of hyperactivity or impulsivity, or do you think you really only struggle significantly with one of those two groups?
I don't really know about... counting them up like that. I've never looked at a checklist. I just know I struggle with both the things you mentioned. I couldn't give you an exact number.

When you think about your daily life, do you feel that your struggles with being disorganized and forgetful are just as frequent and disruptive as your struggles with being restless and blurting things out?
I mean... I guess so. I don't really sit and compare them like that. They're both just... there, I suppose. I couldn't really tell you which one causes more trouble.
